title: Practical Lighting
description: Practical lighting uses a visible or logically present light source within the set as a real contributor: lamps, neon, candles, screens. You see the fixture, and it (or a unit matching it) actually lights the face.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: The set becomes the lighting department. A table lamp in the foreground, a TV, a diner sign: the audience believes the room because the source is in the shot.
Mixed color temperatures are a feature, not a mistake. It is the wrong tool when the fixture is only set dressing and a frontal key from nowhere does the work.
A dark lamp in frame with a face lit from camera is a lie. If the lamp is off-screen but implied, you have shifted toward motivated lighting.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Put working fixtures in frame, often brighter than a real living room so they expose on camera. Control them with bulbs, dimmers, and flags.
Hardness is whatever the shade allows: a bare bulb is hard; a cloth shade is softer. Color is mixed on purpose: tungsten 2700 to 3200K, neon magenta or cyan, screens cooler.
You may hide a small unit in the same shade. Prompt: Practical lighting on [Subject] from visible lamps, neon, candles, or screens in frame, mixed color temperatures, no hidden movie lights.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: Use it when the set should light the face, a night apartment, a bar, a car dash. Do not leave dead props in frame while a beauty key does the real job.

sections.title: Compared with similar shots

blocks.text: Motivated lighting can hide units that match a source; practicals are the sources you see. Candlelight is a specific small warm practical with fast falloff.
Neon practicals are a color-and-sign subset. Available light might include existing fixtures but forbids adding them.
Window light is often a practical architecture plus sky.
Motivated LightingRealism with control. Light like a world, not a studio.

sections.title: In film

blocks.text: Barry Lyndon puts flame in frame as the logic of night. In the Mood for Love and Blade Runner 2049 let lamps, neon, and screens in the set do visible work on faces.
The fixture is part of the composition, not only the plot.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is a dummy lamp plus an off-screen key. The tell is a dark shade and a face lit from the camera.
Fix it by turning the practical up (or matching a hidden unit inside it) and killing the orphan frontal.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is practical lighting in film?
Using visible set fixtures as real lights: lamps, neon, candles, screens. The source is in the world of the shot and it contributes exposure.
Practical lighting vs motivated lighting
Practicals are the fixtures you see. Motivated lighting is the matching logic, which can include hidden units that imitate a window or lamp.
When should I use practical lighting?
Use it when the room should visibly light the people. Skip dummy lamps that do not expose.
How do I prompt practical lighting for AI image or video?
Name visible lamps, neon, candles, or screens as the keys, mixed color temperatures, no hidden movie lights. Say which fixture hits the face.
